The whole-row guard's catalog exemption is whole_row.py:_source_expands_table (line 191): a named Table source does not expand when is_catalog_table(source, dialect=dialect) is true, so a star over it is allowed. is_catalog_table (readonly.py:320-333) returns True when table.db.lower() is in the schemas from _catalog_names(dialect), or when the lowercased name (or the Anonymous function name) startswith the dialect's prefixes. _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT (readonly.py:200-203) has mysql -> schemas {mysql, sys, performance_schema} with no prefixes, and sqlite -> prefixes (sqlite_, pragma_). _catalog_names (212-217) returns the union of all schemas and prefixes for dialect None or an unlisted dialect. claim: Under MySQL with an RLS rule on a table, the RLS guard refuses `SELECT id FROM <view>` with an RlsError matching `view`, and refuses `information_schema.COLUMN_STATISTICS` with an RlsError matching `view`, while allowing information_schema.columns/tables.
verify_hint: Check the RlsError messages raised for views and for value-statistics catalog tables in `verify_base_tables` / the RLS catalog allowlist for mysql.
evidence: Traced by reading only; I did not run the MySQL connector tests. tests/connectors/test_connectors.py:99-100 and 134-145 build RlsGuardRunner(ReadOnlyGuardRunner(RowCapRunner(mysql runner))) and expect RlsError matching 'view'. safety/__init__.py:219 passes require_base_tables=True to the inner runner whenever rules exist. mysql/sql_runner.py:139-140 then calls verify_base_tables(conn, sql, dialect='mysql'). In src/sqllens/safety/relations.py, _verify_relations (lines 155-189) handles each relation. A relation in _METADATA_VIEWS['mysql'] is skipped (lines 163-166). That set (lines 25-32) contains information_schema.columns and information_schema.tables, matched case-insensitively, and the allowed test queries use them. Installed pytest (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_pytest/raises.py): the `raises` overload at line 74-79 types `match: str | re.Pattern[str] | None`; AbstractRaises.__init__ (lines 367-392) only compiles when match is a str, else sets `self.match = match` (None); `_check_match` (line 478-485) returns True when `self.match is None` (type-only check) and otherwise uses `re.search(self.match, stringify_exception(e, ...))`. claim: The comment says that with no dialect the guard applies the union of all denylists (fail-closed), so a MySQL-only function is still refused; the test expects `SELECT load_file('/etc/passwd')` with no dialect to be refused matching "function 'load_file' is not allowed".

        # function must still be refused.
verify_hint: Check `_denied_funcs(None)` in src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py returns the union of every `_SIDE_EFFECT_FUNCS` entry and the refusal message format.
evidence: src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:441-448 `_denied_funcs(None)` returns `_DENIED_UNION` (falsy dialect short-circuits to the union). `_DENIED_UNION` (428-430) = `_ALWAYS_DENIED_FUNCS` unioned with every `_SIDE_EFFECT_FUNCS` value (sqlite + mysql sets, 390-409), which includes 'load_file' (line 399). `assert_select_only` (583-640) calls `_denied_funcs(dialect)` at 624 and walks the tree; `_refuse_denied_function` (555-563) raises UnsafeSqlError with message "function 'load_file' is not allowed: side-effecting / DoS / RCE function refused ...", via `_func_name_candidates` (Anonymous -> node.name.lower(), 465-466). That message matches the test regex "function 'load_file' is not allowed" (tests/unit/test_safety.py:284-288). With dialect None, `_parse_statements` uses base sqlglot Dialect and runs `_mysql_parse_sql`, which has no issue with the '/etc/passwd' literal (no backslashes, no comments). The comment at 285-286 accurately describes this. Caveat: sqlglot source was not available to confirm how base Dialect parses LOAD_FILE (Anonymous vs typed); either way the name candidate would be 'load_file' (sql_names of a typed node would be LOAD_FILE), and the same SQL is already tested for mysql in the parametrized test.

claim: Under dialect mysql, `SELECT md5('sleep')`, `SELECT lower('load_file')` and `SELECT upper('generate_series')` pass assert_select_only: a typed function whose string argument equals a denied name is not refused.
verify_against: src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py denylist candidate-name extraction; sqlglot MySQL parse of MD5/LOWER/UPPER
verify_hint: Check how the denylist walk in src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py derives candidate names from typed exp.Func nodes (it must not use `.name`, which is the first argument) under the mysql dialect.
evidence: Traced assert_select_only (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:583-642) for the three queries under dialect mysql. _parse_statements (537-552) runs _mysql_parse_sql (477-534) first. It raises only on backslash-escaped quotes, /*! or nested comments, and ambiguous double dashes, and none of the three inputs has any of those. It then parses to a single Select. uses_table_shorthand (79-121) finds no TABLE token. The root is a Select, with no INTO and no DML/DDL node. The deny-walk calls _refuse_denied_function on every node (555-563), and that only acts on exp.Func nodes. The string args ('sleep', 'load_file', 'generate_series') are exp.Literal nodes, not Func, so they are never checked. For the function node itself, _func_name_candidates (451-474) takes {node.name.lower()} for exp.Anonymous, whose .name is the written function name (md5/lower/upper). For a typed Func it takes only sql_names() and deliberately does not use .name (the first argument), per the comment at 458-463. sql_names() for MD5/Lower/Upper are MD5 and LOWER/LCASE and UPPER/UCASE. These do not intersect the mysql denylist (_DENIED_BY_DIALECT, 424-427: sleep, load_file, benchmark, sys_exec, sys_eval, get_lock, release_lock, release_all_locks, master_pos_wait, source_pos_wait, plus generate_series and exploding_generate_series), so no exception is raised. The test at tests/unit/test_safety.py:445-449 asserts exactly this. Limits: no dependency_sources were supplied, so I did not read sqlglot's class definitions. The conclusion holds whether sqlglot gives these functions typed nodes or Anonymous nodes, since neither path yields a denied name. I did not run the test.

claim: Under dialect mysql, is_introspection_query returns True for `WITH x AS (SELECT * FROM mysql.user) SELECT * FROM x` (a catalog table inside a CTE still counts).
verify_hint: Trace the SQL through `is_introspection_query` in src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py: the CTE-exclusion scope analysis and whether the `mysql` schema is a MySQL catalog entry.
evidence: Traced by reading, not executed. readonly.py:201 has _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT['mysql'] = ({'mysql','sys','performance_schema'}, ()), so 'mysql' is a catalog schema under dialect mysql (_catalog_names, :212-217). is_introspection_query (:254-317): first_sql_keyword is WITH, not SHOW; parse_one succeeds. _cte_reference_ids (:220-251) marks only unqualified tables whose own name is in scope.cte_sources, which is table `x` in the outer SELECT. The `mysql.user` table has db='mysql', so the `not table.args.get('db')` check excludes it from the CTE-reference set (:238). If normalization or scope analysis raised, the function returns an empty set, which excludes nothing, so the result is the same. The loop at :312-316 skips `x` but reaches `mysql.user`, and is_catalog_table (:320-333) finds table.db.lower()='mysql' in the schemas and returns True. claim: With dialect None, `WITH sqlite_recent AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM sqlite_recent JOIN sqlite_master ON true` is introspection: the union of catalogs under None includes sqlite_master, and the CTE excludes only sqlite_recent.

verify_hint: Check the dialect-None catalog set and prefix rules in src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py and that the generic dialect parses `JOIN ... ON true`.

Lines 207-209 build the prefixes as the union over _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT, i.e. ('sqlite_','pragma_') from line 202, so `sqlite_master` matches via startswith (is_catalog_table, lines 328-333). In is_introspection_query (282-317) dialect None skips the unknown-dialect branch. The first keyword is WITH, not SHOW. parse_one runs under the generic dialect, where `ON true` is an ordinary boolean expression in the JOIN condition. _cte_reference_ids (220-251) excludes only exp.Table nodes with no db/catalog whose name is in scope.cte_sources. That set is just `sqlite_recent`, so the `sqlite_master` table is not excluded and is_catalog_table returns True, giving a True result. If scope analysis raised, it returns an empty set and the result is still True. The test at tests/unit/test_safety.py:785-789 asserts True for this SQL with dialect None. The one residual risk is that I did not execute the generic-dialect parse of `JOIN ... ON true`; I judge it safe from sqlglot's standard parsing.

verify_hint: Trace a SQLite-only catalog (`SELECT name FROM sqlite_master`, `pragma_table_info('t')`) and a MySQL-only one (`mysql.user`, `sys.x`) through `is_introspection_query` with dialect "oracle"; any catalog of either engine not counted falsifies it.
evidence: Docstring at tests/unit/test_safety.py:1231-1232 says that with no dialect, or one with no catalog entry, every remaining engine's catalogs count as introspection. Implementation in src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py: _CATALOGS_BY_DIALECT (200-203) holds exactly mysql ({mysql, sys, performance_schema}) and sqlite (prefixes sqlite_, pragma_), plus _SHARED_CATALOG_SCHEMAS {information_schema} (198). _ALL_CATALOG_SCHEMAS (204-206) and _ALL_CATALOG_NAME_PREFIXES (207-209) are the union over all entries. _catalog_names (212-217) returns that union when dialect is None or .get() finds no entry (e.g. 'oracle'). is_introspection_query (254-317): 'oracle' is a known sqlglot dialect so it is kept; None stays None; an unknown dialect name is reset to None (282-291), so it also takes the union. is_catalog_table (320-333) then checks table.db against the union schemas and the table name, or Anonymous function name for pragma_table_info('t'), against the union prefixes in lowercase. Trace under 'oracle': 'SELECT name FROM sqlite_master' matches prefix sqlite_; 'FROM pragma_table_info(...)' matches pragma_; mysql.user / sys.x / performance_schema.t match the schema set; information_schema matches the shared set. Absolute-claim input traced: a MySQL-only catalog (mysql.user) and a SQLite-only catalog (pragma_table_info('t')) under dialect 'oracle'; both are counted, so no engine catalog is dropped. Existing tests agree (test_safety.py:903-905, 921-935, 944-949). The CTE-shadow exclusion (311-314) is the documented rule and is not a catalog. Note: the test class itself only exercises performance_schema and information_schema under None/oracle, a narrower test than the docstring, but the docstring's claim is true of the code.

claim: The comment asserts that MySQL's `TABLE orders` means `SELECT * FROM orders` and that apply_rls refuses it on every sqlglot version, whatever its parse.
source_excerpt:
# MySQL `TABLE orders` is semantically `SELECT * FROM orders`; it is
        # refused on every sqlglot version, whatever its parse. Fail-secure.
verify_against: apply_rls in src/sqllens/safety/rls.py and uses_table_shorthand in src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py; MySQL 8.0 TABLE statement semantics
verify_hint: Check that apply_rls runs the tokenizer-based TABLE shorthand check before relying on any parse. Falsifying inputs to trace: `TABLE orders` written with a comment before it, or a mixed-case `Table orders`, under dialect mysql.
evidence: apply_rls (src/sqllens/safety/rls.py:206-210) calls uses_table_shorthand(sql, dialect) before sqlglot.parse (line 213), so no parse is relied on for TABLE; it raises RlsError 'unquoted TABLE keyword'. uses_table_shorthand (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:79-121) tokenizes with the dialect's tokenizer and returns True for any token of TokenType.TABLE whose previous token is not in the exclusion set (CREATE, DROP, ALTER, DESCRIBE, SHOW, EXPLAIN, etc.). Falsifying inputs traced: (1) comment before, e.g. '/* c */ TABLE orders' or '-- c\nTABLE orders': comments are attached to tokens by the tokenizer and are not tokens, so previous stays '' and TABLE is flagged. (2) mixed-case 'Table orders': token type is TABLE regardless of case (the code compares token_type, not text), and the test covers 'table orders'. A leading-position TABLE (previous '' ) is never excluded. The exclusion list only suppresses cases where TABLE follows DDL/utility keywords (those are exp.Command and refused by the non-Query check at rls.py:228 anyway); none of them can legally precede a TABLE query in a read. Docstring at readonly.py:82-85 states the same version-independence reason. MySQL 8.0 documents TABLE t as equivalent to SELECT * FROM t, so the comment's semantics are accurate. The test at tests/unit/test_safety_rls.py:355-362 exercises 'TABLE orders' and 'table orders' under mysql.
